value.0: Thermal Detonator's closed on my ledger, and yours is the only name signed clean at the bottom of it. Every charge you set from here on, I want it built like I'm still standing behind you counting fingers.
Not yet. I don't badge civilians into a live range on reputation. Come back when Devices work is reflex for you, not something you're still counting through on your fingers.

That marker you just walked past means live ordinance, and you strolled by it like it was a fence post. Second one today. First one's the reason Hutlar Qion Test Site is locked to everyone but me: there's a crew in there cooking oversized charges with no containment plan, and I am done finding their mistakes after the fact. Put down six of their adepts in the test site on Hutlar, and bring me back a Thermal Detonator Qion Test Log so I know exactly what they were building before it built itself into a crater.
Good. Don't touch anything marked, don't skip a step because it looks finished, and don't come back until you can hand me the log instead of an excuse.

Because the last crew that got sloppy here took out two range walls and a supply shed with them. I sealed Hutlar Qion Test Site the same week and haven't unsealed it since. Whoever's in there now, I want their names before I want their heads.
Charges built past rated yield, no containment casing, no logged fuze timing. That is not testing, that is gambling with a blast radius. I want the log that tells me how far they pushed it.
Everything I need and nothing I want to hear. Fuze curve, yield estimate, whoever signed off on it. Bring it back whole; a torn page tells me less than no page at all.
Hutlar Qion Test Site still owes me that Test Log. Six adepts down, log in hand, then we talk.
That's the log I asked for. Hand it here before you lose a finger carrying it wrong.
Six adepts and an honest log, first day. Credits are hazard pay. The lesson is that Thermal Detonator answers to paperwork before it answers to you.

The log you brought me raised more questions than it answered. Their specialists are running a cryo-range regulator hot enough to crack, and if that thing lets go near the test wells it won't be a training accident, it'll be a funeral. Go back to Hutlar Qion Test Site, drop five of their specialists, and bring me the regulator before it decides for itself when it's done.
A day I don't have, but fine. Go when you're ready, and go careful. That regulator doesn't warn you before it lets go.
Cryo-shatter, not a clean burn. It sprays supercooled shrapnel through anyone standing near it, then whatever's left cooks off anyway. I've buried range hands for less.
Because pushing yield past spec is the only way their numbers make their masters happy. I've seen it before. It never ends with the regulator; it ends with the person holding it.
Strip it down on my bench, find out how far past spec they pushed it, and use that number to keep the next fool honest. Small mercy, but it's the one I've got.
That regulator is still ticking down in Hutlar Qion Test Site. Five specialists, one regulator, then back here.
You're still standing, so the regulator behaved. Hand it over before your luck changes its mind.
Cold, intact, and thoroughly incriminating. You're starting to look less like a liability and more like someone I can send back in without losing sleep over it.

Their warden's been running that site like a private range, and frostburn scarring on the last crest we recovered says the tests are getting bigger, not smaller. I am not sending you at that alone. Bring two people you'd trust to carry a live charge, go to Hutlar Qion Test Site, put the warden down, and bring me back the Frostburned Test Crest.
Good, go find them. A test site is not a duel, and the warden doesn't fight like one either.
Because the last one who tried it solo, I found in three pieces and none of them near each other. One set of hands can't watch a blast radius and a warden at the same time. Two more sets can.

It's frostburned, which means whatever the warden's setting off now runs colder and meaner than anything on the books. I want that crest to know what I'm dealing with before it becomes everyone's problem.
Detonators staged in pairs, timed to catch whoever survives the first one. Ugly, efficient, exactly the kind of lesson I'd teach if I'd gone the wrong way with this work.
The warden and that crest are still waiting in Hutlar Qion Test Site. Don't go back in without the company I told you to bring.
You're walking, and so is your crew, apparently. Hand over the crest and let's see what frostburn actually looks like up close.
That's a warden down and a crest that'll keep me up reading it tonight. You didn't do that with a will and a prayer, you did it with backup. Remember that.

The warden was muscle. The inner circle is the ones who signed off on using him that way. I want their Site Chief's Override Chip; it'll tell me who authorized what, and there's no version of that list I like the look of. Four of them, Hutlar Qion Test Site, bring the chip back whole.
Then go. Four names on that chip is four fewer people I have to guess about.
Every override past safety lockout, timestamped and signed. That chip is a confession that doesn't know it's one yet.
On paper, nobody. In practice, whoever the warden answered to, and whoever they answer to still hasn't shown their face. I have a guess, and I don't like it.
Wouldn't hurt. Four of them together is worse odds than one warden alone, even if none of them hit as hard.
That override chip is still sitting in Hutlar Qion Test Site with four people standing on top of it. Go get it.
Four down and a chip in hand. Let's see exactly how deep this goes.
Deep enough that I'm glad I sent you instead of going myself. One name left on this list, and it's the one that matters.

That chip led exactly where I didn't want it to: the site's master, and he doesn't run tests anymore, he runs Thermal Detonator the way I taught it before I knew better. He'll drop more ordinance in thirty seconds than the whole crew combined, aimed at whoever's still standing closest together. Don't go in with fewer than three. This is the last lesson, and there's no partial credit on it.
Take it. Come back with two people who trust you and a plan you actually believe in, not just the one that sounded good standing here.
The warden staged charges. The master reads a room and places them where the room will actually be standing, which is worse. He's not testing ordinance anymore, he's testing people.
Because I trained half his methods into people who never should have kept them. Thermal Detonator was supposed to end with better range discipline than this. Instead it ended with him.
Then the site's mine again, and Thermal Detonator's yours. I don't hand that over to just anyone, and I'm not planning to regret handing it to you.
He's still down there, and I'm not sending you back in short-handed. Bring your two, then go.
You're standing, he's not, and Hutlar Qion Test Site just got a lot quieter. That's all the proof I needed.
Then it's done properly, for the first time in longer than I'd like to admit. Thermal Detonator is yours now. Set your charges cleaner than the fools who made me lock this place down.
Back to the proof.
I'll count the charges for you.
Why is the range locked down in the first place?
What is this crew actually building in there?
What will the test log tell you?
Not yet. I've got other business.
Here's the log.
Back to the proof.
I'll bring it back before it fails.
What happens if the regulator cracks?
Why are specialists running it hot?
What will you do with the regulator once I bring it?
Give me a day first.
Here's the regulator, still in one piece.
Back to the proof.
I'll bring company.
Why can't I handle the warden alone?
What does the crest prove?
What's this warden's specialty?
I need to find people first.
Here's the crest.
Back to the proof.
I'll get you that chip.
What's on an override chip like that?
Who's actually running this site?
Should I bring the same crew back?
Not right now.
Here's the chip.
Back to the proof.
I'm going in, and I'm not going alone.
What makes him different from the warden?
Why do you know his methods so well?
What happens after he's down?
I need more time before that fight.
It's done. He's down.
